description: Find duplicate keys in one dataset, exactly and nearly. An exact duplicate is reported with every row it occupies. A near duplicate is two different keys that become identical once case, spacing or punctuation is set aside, which a unique index accepts and which is almost always the same entity entered twice. Keys are canonicalised exactly, so 42 and 42.0 are one key. Pay 100000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

csv.description: The dataset to check. Delimited text with a header row, at most 262144 bytes and 5000 data rows. RFC 4180 quoting is honoured. Nothing is fetched.
csv.example:
email,signed_up
Ada@Example.test,2026-01-01
ada@example.test,2026-02-01
ada@example.test ,2026-03-01
grace@example.test,2026-01-05
grace@example.test,2026-04-01

delimiter.description: Single field separator. Defaults to a comma.

key.description: The columns forming the key. A composite key is supported. Values are canonicalised exactly, so 42 and 42.0 are the same key and a large identifier is compared as text rather than collapsed.

normalise.description: Transformations applied only for near-duplicate detection, never to the exact comparison.

name: duplicate_key_audit

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of the data was not, which is a different problem from data that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

row.description: 1-based and counting the header, so it matches a text editor.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

unique.description: True only when the dataset was fully read and no key repeated exactly or near-identically.

title: Duplicate Key Audit
